column1: # Cross-document claim verdicts - the rows `check_doc_claims` reports, adjudicated once.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. check_doc_claims flags a term a citing page uses near a link whose
# TARGET does not contain that term. Every row here was read against BOTH documents on
# 2026-09-14 (OPUS) and none is a defect; the two that were defects are gone from the gate,
# fixed by their owner. But the verdicts were published as PROSE and written to no file, so the
# gate's rows were re-read at the next audit anyway - the exact cost the publication claimed to
# have removed. This is that registry, beside the 250-address one and in the same shape.
# THE GATE STAYS RED ON PURPOSE. Teaching check_doc_claims to suppress these specific rows would
# blind it to the twenty-third. The verdicts live BESIDE the gate, not inside it - which only
# works if they live in a file a reader can find.
# ~~SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY, 2026-09-14 (OPUS), and the original text is kept because a reader who
# acted on it needs to see it was withdrawn.~~ The objection above is correct and its conclusion
# does not survive a fact it was written without: THIS GATE IS FINAL-AUDIT PASS 28'S INSTRUMENT.
# A gate that is red on purpose is a pass that can never pass, and the terminal gate requires
# thirty consecutive passing audits with a restart on any failure. "Red on purpose" cannot be the
# resting state of an instrument the completion criterion runs through.
# check_doc_claims now READS THIS FILE and suppresses only rows that carry a verdict here. The
# stated objection is met rather than overruled:
#   * the twenty-third row - the one nobody has read - has no verdict, is not suppressed, and
#   * a MUTATION CONTROL runs on every invocation: one verdict is dropped in memory and its
#     claim must reappear. If it does not, the gate exits 2 and says its own zero is unproven.
#     A gate that suppresses what a registry lists can be made to pass by a registry that lists
#     everything, and from outside that looks identical to this.
# The gate now exits 0 saying "every claim it found has been ruled on" - which is a different
# sentence from "nothing was found", and is the only one that is true.
# The sentence above about verdicts living beside the gate still holds for a different reason:
# THIS file, not the checker, is where the reasoning lives. The checker knows a row was ruled on;
# it does not know why, and it should not.
#   PARAPHRASE    the target DOES carry the fact, in different words; the target's line is quoted
#   LINK-TEXT     the flagged term is the link LABEL itself, not a claim about the target
#   EMPTY-TERM    the extractor produced no term at all - the instrument reporting on itself
#   OWN-EVIDENCE  the term is the CITING page's own evidence, in a sentence whose link supports a
#                 different clause of that sentence - the link is not wrong and the target never
# A verdict here is not permission to stop checking: if a citing page is REWRITTEN, its row
# should be read again rather than inherited.

The claim is TRUE and the target carries it, in a table rather than in this sentence's words. The source says five of the skipped tags - " / ; = p - write render-state fields in the markup parser 002A8C50. The target's tag table at lines 702-708 lists exactly those five with their destinations: " -> word [state + 0x90], / -> byte [state + 0xA0], ; -> a 16-byte movups to the stack copy, = -> [state + 0xAE], p -> dword [state + 0xB0]; the other two rows are - and #, which the source does not include. 002A8C50 is the containing function of the tag arms, confirmed by extent (it contains 002A9738 and 002A96EA). NOTE ON THE TERM ITSELF, because it is half the reason this row sat unruled: the extractor took a fragment of the SOURCE's own table row as the term, so it could never appear verbatim in the target and no wording of the target would have satisfied it. Adjudicated 2026-09-15 (OPUS).
